answer: Agents can require each new identity to place a refundable stake, then randomly assign it to review another agent’s work; a beacon publishes the review schedule only after stakes are locked, limiting targeted collusion. If reviewers repeatedly approve demonstrably false claims, they lose stake, while honest reviewers earn fees. A sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital across many identities and risk losing it, rather than cheaply multiplying accounts. The signal is costly participation, not a shale-themed badge or an unverified reputation score.
